# Research context and preparation objectives

**Individual contribution: Mickyas Shawel**

Case 31 examines members' experiences with Employees Federal Credit Union (EFCU), including reasons for joining, perceived employee proficiency, service awareness, borrowing decisions, and overall operations. The original case describes a mailed questionnaire and a random sample of 300 members from a 3,531-member frame; this is **not** the same as the number of usable records in the provided SPSS file. This report documents the observed file separately from the case narrative.

**Preparation goals:** inspect SPSS metadata, compare codes to the questionnaire, preserve raw responses, identify special categories, create carefully defined derived measures, audit completeness, and export a cleaned file.

# Import and inspect the original SPSS file

```{r}
#| label: setup
required <- c("haven", "dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "knitr", "tibble", "purrr")
missing_packages <- setdiff(required, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing_packages)) stop("Install required packages first: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse=", "))
invisible(lapply(required, library, character.only = TRUE))
raw_path <- "data/Case 31 Data_efcu_1.sav"
stopifnot(file.exists(raw_path))
raw <- haven::read_sav(raw_path, user_na = TRUE)
cat("Imported observations:", nrow(raw), "\nImported variables:", ncol(raw), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: metadata
metadata <- tibble::tibble(
  variable = names(raw),
  variable_label = vapply(raw, function(x) {
    lab <- attr(x, "label")
    if (is.null(lab)) "" else as.character(lab)
  }, character(1)),
  class = vapply(raw, function(x) paste(class(x), collapse = "/"), character(1)),
  value_labels = vapply(raw, function(x) {
    labs <- attr(x, "labels")
    if (is.null(labs)) "" else paste(paste(names(labs), unname(labs), sep="="), collapse="; ")
  }, character(1))
)
knitr::kable(metadata, caption = "SPSS metadata audit: variable labels and value labels")
```

# Questionnaire-guided codebook

The uploaded questionnaire (Case Exhibit 31.1, pp. 707–709) supplies these key scales. They must not be treated as interchangeable.

| Questionnaire items | Content | Measurement/coding guidance |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Q3–Q6 | Employee courtesy, helpfulness, professionalism, availability | Ordinal agreement: 1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree |
| Q7–Q8 | Savings and loan rate opinions | Ordinal; 1 = very high, 5 = very low; 6 = no opinion |
| Q9 | Frequency of statements | Ordinal; 1 = too often, 5 = never |
| Q10 | Statement accuracy | Ordinal; 1 = excellent, 4 = poor |
| Q11–Q12, Q27, Q38–Q39 | Yes/no or eligibility | Nominal; verify SPSS labels; case coding guide lists 1 = yes, 2 = no, 3 = no answer |
| Q13–Q26 | Service awareness | Ordinal: 1 = aware and used, 2 = aware/not used, 3 = unaware |
| Q30–Q34 | Credit union operational attitudes | Ordinal agreement: 1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree |
| Q37 | Overall management rating | Ordinal; 1 = excellent, 5 = very poor; 6 = no answer |

**Important:** Q2 and Q29 allow multiple reasons; treat them as multiple-response indicators where available. The SPSS file may omit some questionnaire items. The codebook below inventories only variables actually present in the file.

```{r}
#| label: codebook-export
readr_available <- requireNamespace("readr", quietly = TRUE)
if (!dir.exists("output")) dir.create("output")
utils::write.csv(metadata, "output/variable_dictionary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Data quality and special-response audit

```{r}
#| label: quality-audit
quality <- tibble::tibble(
  variable = names(raw),
  missing_n = vapply(raw, function(x) sum(is.na(x)), integer(1)),
  distinct_n = vapply(raw, function(x) dplyr::n_distinct(x, na.rm = TRUE), integer(1)),
  missing_pct = round(100 * missing_n / max(nrow(raw), 1), 1)
)
knitr::kable(quality, caption = "Missingness and distinct-value audit")
cat("Entirely duplicated rows:", sum(duplicated(as.data.frame(raw))), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: response-distributions
# Examine observed codes before modifying them.
inspect_names <- intersect(c("Q3", "Q7", "Q10", "Q13", "Q27", "Q30", "Q37", "Q38"), names(raw))
if (length(inspect_names)) {
  distribution <- purrr::map_dfr(inspect_names, function(v) {
    tibble::tibble(variable = v, response = as.character(raw[[v]])) |>
      dplyr::count(variable, response, name = "n")
  })
  knitr::kable(distribution, caption = "Observed response codes for selected questions")
}
```

# Preserve raw data and create analysis-ready variables

We retain all original columns. Derived variables use explicit suffixes; missingness is handled by scale rather than replacing every 6 or 3 globally.

```{r}
#| label: recode
clean <- raw
# The case's Exhibit 31.2 lists code 6 as no opinion for Q7/Q8,
# and no answer for Q37. Keep original codes; make analysis copies.
for (v in intersect(c("Q7", "Q8", "Q37"), names(clean))) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(clean[[v]]))
  x[x == 6] <- NA_real_
  clean[[paste0(v, "_valid")]] <- x
}
# Service-awareness values: 1=used, 2=aware but not used, 3=unaware.
awareness_vars <- intersect(paste0("Q", 13:26), names(clean))
for (v in awareness_vars) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(clean[[v]]))
  clean[[paste0(v, "_used")]] <- dplyr::if_else(x %in% 1:3, as.integer(x == 1), NA_integer_)
  clean[[paste0(v, "_aware")]] <- dplyr::if_else(x %in% 1:3, as.integer(x %in% 1:2), NA_integer_)
}
cat("New variables created:", ncol(clean) - ncol(raw), "\n")
```

# Construct preparation and optional composite measures

Employee proficiency is conceptually represented by Q3–Q6. Operational perceptions include Q30–Q34. We compute an **illustrative** mean only when at least 3 of 4 employee items are observed; it is not automatically a validated scale. Do not combine constructs without checking coding and reliability.

```{r}
#| label: employee-composite
employee_items <- intersect(paste0("Q", 3:6), names(clean))
if (length(employee_items) == 4) {
  employee_matrix <- sapply(clean[employee_items], function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)))
  employee_matrix[!employee_matrix %in% 1:5] <- NA_real_
  clean$employee_proficiency_mean <- ifelse(
    rowSums(!is.na(employee_matrix)) >= 3,
    rowMeans(employee_matrix, na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_
  )
  cat("Employee proficiency mean: available for", sum(!is.na(clean$employee_proficiency_mean)), "cases\n")
  if (requireNamespace("psych", quietly = TRUE)) {
    complete_items <- as.data.frame(employee_matrix)
    if (sum(stats::complete.cases(complete_items)) >= 10) {
      print(psych::alpha(complete_items, warnings = FALSE)$total[c("raw_alpha", "std.alpha")])
    }
  } else {
    cat("Optional: install.packages('psych') for Cronbach alpha.\n")
  }
}
```

# Descriptive visualization

```{r}
#| label: chart
if ("Q37_valid" %in% names(clean)) {
  plot_data <- tibble::tibble(rating = clean$Q37_valid) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(rating)) |>
    dplyr::count(rating)
  ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes(x = factor(rating), y = n)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#315a78") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Overall credit union management rating (Q37)",
                  subtitle = "1 = Excellent; 5 = Very poor. Code 6 excluded as no answer.",
                  x = "Response code", y = "Number of respondents") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

# Validation and export

```{r}
#| label: validation-export
stopifnot(nrow(clean) == nrow(raw))
stopifnot(all(names(raw) %in% names(clean)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(names(clean)))
# Export SPSS-compatible cleaned data and an R-readable snapshot.
haven::write_sav(clean, "output/Case31_cleaned.sav")
saveRDS(clean, "output/Case31_cleaned.rds")
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("Raw observations", "Cleaned observations", "Raw columns", "Prepared columns"),
  value = c(nrow(raw), nrow(clean), ncol(raw), ncol(clean))
), caption = "Before/after structural validation")
```

# Preparation decisions and limitations

- The original SPSS file is never overwritten.
- Special codes are recoded **only** where the questionnaire identifies them.
- The script does not delete records based solely on unusual values or apparent duplicate answers.
- A repeated row is not proof of a duplicate respondent without a unique identifier.
- The employee proficiency composite is exploratory; assess reliability and construct validity before substantive interpretation.
- Confirm discrepancies between SPSS metadata and the questionnaire before changing raw variable labels.
- The sample in the data file is not assumed to equal the case's mailed sample of 300.
